messages:
maya: Quick thread: post-launch tidy-up. We have 9 items flagged by CS + telemetry. Need a deterministic rule: do we run a 2-week surgical patch sprint for top regressions OR roll a feature-wave that includes some fixes? I sketched options in the board: https://tiny.redwood/backlog

ajay: Prefer surgical patch for the ones that hit core paths. Feature work can wait unless it's a contract deliverable.

courtney: Proposed triage matrix:
```
Blocker = data loss / crash -> immediate hotfix
High = core flow broken for >0.5% DAU or named customer -> hotfix
Medium = perf/UX degradation -> next sprint
Low = polish/requests -> backlog
```
Also mark "regression" tickets +1 severity.

ben: Add: any DB-affecting fix needs a safety owner and smoke script.

sara: I'll own rollout + smoke scripts for hotfixes. Can we reserve a Thu morning canary slot?

oliver: For enhancements, tag fast-wins (<=3 dev days) vs invest (>3d). Fast-wins go in the first follow-up wave.

dena: CS asks for ETA on two customer-facing fixes. If we pick surgical patch, I can promise a calendar week ETA.

maya: Decision proposal: lock a 2-week patch sprint for items with "High" or "Blocker" only. Owners: ajay, ben, sara. Fast-win enhancements (<=3d) may be scheduled into the sprint if they unblock customers and have owner sign-off. Longer feature work goes into next planning cycle or the "strategic buffer".

ajay: I'll take cache invalidation and profile corruption. Ben takes search ranking and paging. Sara runs rollout.

courtney: I'll add acceptance criteria fields to enhancement tickets: metric or UX screenshot required.

release-bot: Canary booked: Thu 09:00-10:00 UTC for team product-patch. Label PRs `patch/canary` and include smoke logs.

maya: Action items: 1) Owners add short rollout + estimate to each ticket by EOD. 2) Dena will notify impacted customers once owners confirm. 3) Sara to publish smoke script template. We'll re-check Friday to confirm canary readiness. :white_check_mark:
